name: Krishna Dvaipayana Vyasadeva
summary: He is the legendary sage and primary compiler of the Vedic scriptures who serves as the narrator and central figure in the composition of the Srimad Bhagavata.

name: Sukadeva Goswami
summary: Sukadeva Goswami is the illustrious and realized sage who narrates the Srimad Bhagavatam to King Pariksit, delivering profound spiritual wisdom and the glories of the Supreme Lord.

name: Vishnu
summary: Mahavishnu is the plenary expansion of the Supreme Lord who lies within the Causal Ocean and exhales the innumerable universes during the process of cosmic manifestation.

name: Naimisaranya
summary: An ancient and sacred forest where great sages, led by Shaunaka Rishi, gathered to perform long-term sacrifices and hear the recitation of the Puranas.

name: Saunaka Rishi
summary: He is the chief of the sages assembled in the forest of Naimisaranya who inquires about the Supreme Truth from Suta Gosvami.

name: Brahma-satra
summary: A Brahma-satra refers to a prolonged 1000 year sacrificial gathering or assembly of sages dedicated to the attainment of spiritual knowledge and the welfare of the world.

name: Suta Goswami
summary: A learned orator and disciple of Vyasadeva who narrates the Puranic scriptures to the assembled sages in the forest of Naimisaranya.

name: Kali-yuga
summary: The fourth and final epoch in the cycle of yugas, characterized by a decline in spiritual knowledge, virtue, and righteousness.

name: Vasudeva
summary: Vasudeva is the noble prince of the Yadu dynasty and the father of Lord Krishna, known for his unwavering adherence to righteousness and truth.

name: Devaki
summary: Devaki is the wife of Vasudeva and the mother of Lord Krishna, revered as a pivotal figure in the Bhagavata Purana for her divine role in the Lord's manifestation.

name: Ganges
summary: The sacred river flowing from the lotus feet of Lord Vishnu, revered for its purifying spiritual power and its role in sanctifying the terrestrial realm.

name: Kalas
summary: Kalas refer to the sixteen fractional manifestations or divine potencies of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, representing His transcendental qualities and energies.

name: Brahma
summary: Brahma is the secondary creator of the universe within the cosmic order, tasked by the Supreme Lord with the manifestation of the material world and its living beings.

name: Shiva
summary: Lord Shiva, the supreme deity responsible for the dissolution of the universe within the Vedic cosmology described in the Srimad Bhagavata.

name: Lilavatara
summary: These are the various forms assumed by the Supreme Lord specifically to perform transcendental pastimes within the material world for the pleasure of His devotees and the maintenance of cosmic order.

name: Rama
summary: Rama is the seventh avatar of Lord Vishnu, known as the ideal man and king who upholds righteousness and moral law.

name: Krishna
summary: The eighth Avatara of Lord Vishnu who descends into the material world to protect the righteous and restore cosmic order.

name: Dharma
summary: Dharma refers to the eternal, universal laws of duty, righteousness, and order that sustain the cosmos and guide the moral conduct of all living beings.

name: Romaharshana Suta
summary: A learned disciple of Veda Vyasa who is renowned for his expertise in reciting the Puranas and serves as the primary narrator for the assembly of sages at Naimisharanya.

name: Samsara
summary: Samsara refers to the continuous cycle of birth, death, and rebirth within the material world which the soul undergoes until attaining spiritual liberation.

name: Nara-Narayana Rsi
summary: Nara and Narayana are the twin incarnations of the Supreme Personality of Godhead who reside in Badarikashrama performing severe penances for the benefit of all living entities.

name: Sarasvati
summary: Sarasvati is the Vedic goddess of knowledge, music, arts, wisdom, and learning, often venerated as the consort of Lord Brahma.
